label: alg:delta-lambda-closure
title: $\Delta_\lambda$ per-partition value (PROVED $(-1)^{n(\lambda)}\dim V_\lambda$); many-body magnitude open
html:
Algorithm (\Delta_\lambda per-partition value — PROVED; many-body magnitude — open). Compute the per-partition binding weight \Delta_\lambda(K) for an isotope knot K, consumed by Step 9b (alg:per-isotope-binding).

Input

  • Isotope knot K + braid index n_K.
  • Partition \lambda \vdash n_K.

Output

  • Per-partition weight \Delta_\lambda = (-1)^{n(\lambda)}\dim V_\lambda \in \mathbb{Z} (the signed Springer dimension; n(\lambda) is the jet-order valuation parity, \dim V_\lambda the Wedderburn dimension).

Status: value proved, magnitude external

The per-partition value is PROVED, sorry-free, general-n: \Delta_\lambda = (-1)^{n(\lambda)}\dim V_\lambda (QOU.BraidsAndKnots.dtEuler_eq_deltaLambda_unconditional; value + chirality sign, no n \le 5 restriction). The sign leg is the jet-order valuation parity deltaSign_eq_nStat_parity; the magnitude leg is the Wedderburn dimension. Both are substrate-derived — not fitted.

What remains open is NOT the value — it is the many-body binding MAGNITUDE. The six ansätze recorded below failed to derive the deuteron/light-nucleus magnitude deficit r^\ast \approx 1.585, not the per-partition value. This is a category distinction the old framing conflated:

  • Proved (value): \Delta_\lambda = (-1)^{n(\lambda)}\dim V_\lambda.
  • Open (magnitude): the additive extensive term. A per-block weight \Delta_\lambda cannot supply it — the trace binding B = E_0\,\Delta\mathrm{tr}_M is intensive, and no per-block weight can convert an intensive quantity into an extensive one. The pairwise log-det cumulant is likewise proved-capped at A = 4: \rho_4 \le C(4,2) = 6, while strong targets need \rho_4 \approx 13 > 6 (QOU.MassTheory.exchangeDet_pow_two_le_four, sorry-free), so the missing term is super-pairwise (irreducibly \ge 3-body). The cap is stated for general A as \rho_A \le C(A,2) in that file's header, but what is proved there is the single determinant inequality (1-m^2)^6 \le (1+3m)(1-m)^3 on [0,1], which is the A = 4 instance and the only theorem the file contains. The exclusion argument needs no more than that, since it is run at the deuteron and ^4\mathrm{He}; a general-A cap would be a stronger result and is not currently in the corpus.

Historical: the six refuted magnitude ansätze

These attempted to force the many-body magnitude into \Delta_\lambda; all were refuted on the deuteron (each supplied the wrong r^\ast, none touched the now-proved value):

Ansatz Source Refuted on
Frobenius co-Casimir early Frobenius-pairing proposals deuteron
Demazure-fibre symmetric-crystal early attempts deuteron
LP-Plancherel LP-based ansatz deuteron
LP-Frobenius LP-based ansatz deuteron
crystal-graph naïve KLR / Kashiwara level-0 deuteron
augmented Markov Markov-extension ansatz deuteron

Correctness conditions

rem:term6-binding-density fixes the binding sum's algebraic shape. The per-partition weight is now the closed form (-1)^{n(\lambda)}\dim V_\lambda; the open piece is the separate, super-pairwise extensive magnitude term (see Status).

Witness contract

Per-partition \Delta_\lambda values (the proved closed form) are emitted to computations/delta-lambda-witness.json, consumed by binding_K_direct.py. The witness carries the VALUE only — the binding total additionally requires the y_\lambda\,\chi^\lambda weighting and the separate extensive magnitude term (open).

Notes

The per-partition value is now proved; the magnitude is not, and six fit-based ansätze have failed on it. A seventh fit would not advance the question: under the three-calibration discipline a fitted magnitude is not a derivation. The magnitude is a separate additive extensive term (super-pairwise), and remains open.
